description: SMART-DS (Synthetic Models for Advanced, Realistic Testing: Distribution systems and Scenarios) is a set of realistic large-scale US electrical distribution models from the National Laboratory of the Rockies, formerly NREL, for testing grid algorithms and technology analysis. The entry on the DOE Open Energy Data Portal, read on 2026-09-26, describes synthetic detailed distribution network models with connected time series loads for the greater San Francisco, Greensboro and Austin areas, validated against thousands of utility feeders for statistical and operational similarity to US networks, in OpenDSS format and split into zipped regions, with a user guide. The entry was last modified on 2 January 2024 and is licensed CC BY 4.0, free of charge. Caveats: the networks are synthetic, not real utility assets, and the entry links out, not holding records. Simulation uses are large-scale network flow and hosting capacity studies, capacity planning and resilience tests of distribution automation. Related records: data-ieee-pes-distribution-test-feeders gives smaller standard feeders, and platform-altdss-dss-c-api runs OpenDSS models.
